title: The 1926 Slavery Convention’s Centennial in Context
summary_en: What do you do when you realize moral failure has underwritten your life? This is the story beyond the 1926 Slavery Convention, which was deeply imperfect, but 100 years ago constituted the international community's first attempt at ending the moral scourge of slavery.
title_cn: The 1926 Slavery Convention’s Centennial in Context

title: Xi Jinping’s Return to Washington: A State Visit to Build Stability
summary_en: Xi’s visit to Washington is likely to be heavy on optics and symbolism but light on substantive progress, highlighting both leaders’ conviction that each is the only one who can manage the other and that regular meetings are necessary to stabilize the bilateral relationship.
title_cn: Xi Jinping’s Return to Washington: A State Visit to Build Stability

title: He Said, Xi Said
summary_en: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses potential outcomes of the upcoming summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington.

title: What Iran and Ukraine Reveal About OSINT in War
summary_en: The war with Iran and Russia's war on Ukraine hold a critical lesson for the United States: just how little control it may have over how foreign adversaries collect and exploit open-source intelligence against its interests.
title_cn: What Iran and Ukraine Reveal About OSINT in War

title: Understanding the U.S. Federal Government’s AI Spending
summary_en: Federal agencies obligated $4.1 billion across 2,255 AI-related contracts since FY 2019, and 83 percent of those dollars went to the Defense Department. The CSIS Futures Lab follows the money trail and tracks the evolution of federal AI demand.
title_cn: Understanding the U.S. Federal Government’s AI Spending

title: The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit
summary_en: In a new report, Chris Collins and Aalok Mehta analyze the global AI governance landscape and outline how Washington should approach AI talks at the upcoming U.S.-China summit.
title_cn: The State of AI Global Governance and Its Implications for the U.S.-China Summit

title: The Levantine Opportunity in a Churning Middle East
summary_en: The wars of the past three years have eroded the fragile order of the Middle East. Now, for the first time in decades, the Levant has a chance to create a new alignment and build a regional order centered around strong, inclusive states, stability, and open trade.
title_cn: The Levantine Opportunity in a Churning Middle East

title: What Would an Interim U.S.-Mexico Trade Deal Actually Involve?
summary_en: Mexico is close to an interim deal with the United States. What it concedes for tariff relief today could set the baseline for North America down the line.
title_cn: What Would an Interim U.S.-Mexico Trade Deal Actually Involve?

title: Rethinking Export Controls as a Tool in Modern Technology Competition
summary_en: Export controls can delay China’s technological progress, but they cannot secure lasting U.S. leadership. This report examines the limits and costs of semiconductor controls and argues for pairing targeted restrictions with sustained investment in U.S. innovation.
title_cn: Rethinking Export Controls as a Tool in Modern Technology Competition

title: Behind the Headlines: What Motivates and Moves Japanese Elite Opinion on Nuclear Weapons Acquisition
summary_en: A CSIS Japan Chair survey shows that the majority of Japanese strategic elites oppose nuclear weapons acquisition despite a worsening security environment—but these attitudes could shift if South Korea acquires the bomb or the United States reduces its military presence.
title_cn: Behind the Headlines: What Motivates and Moves Japanese Elite Opinion on Nuclear Weapons Acquisition
